note: One shared glossary. `plain` is the wording the story uses; `term` is the exact technical term shown on hover/tap with `def`. Every factual definition cites quotes that scripts/07_build_glossary.py checks word for word against the source text (a Q&A passage in qa_chunks.json or a committed file). Entries with no factual claim (a unit or a plain re-wording) say so in `kind`.

us_std_atm_1976.citation: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976. NOAA, NASA and U.S. Air Force, NOAA-S/T 76-1562 / NASA-TM-X-74335 (NTRS 19770009539).
us_std_atm_1976.use: Altitude companions for pressures in the story: lower atmosphere (0-11 km) P = 101.325 kPa x (1 + L h / T0)^(-g0 M0 / (R* L)), with T0 = 288.15 K, L = -0.0065 K/m, g0 = 9.80665 m/s2, M0 = 0.0289644 kg/mol, R* = 8.31432 J/(mol K); 11-20 km isothermal at 216.65 K from 22.632 kPa. Height is geopotential (differs from geometric height by < 0.2% below 11 km); shown rounded to 100 m.

terms.plain: more oxygen makes materials burn more easily
terms.def: Moon-base air is planned at 30% oxygen or more, over 40% more than Earth's air, which makes materials much more flammable. NASA prevents fires partly by choosing materials, which depends on knowing their flammability limits.

quotes.quote: Compared to Earth’s atmosphere, that’s more than a 40% increase in the oxygen concentration making materials much more flammable
quotes.label: challenge page

quotes.quote: Prevention is achieved by controlling ignition sources and through material selection, which depends on understanding flammability limits
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: acrylic plastic
terms.def: PMMA (polymethylmethacrylate) is acrylic plastic. BASS-II burned it as rods, slabs and thin films.

quotes.quote: PMMA polymethylmethacrylate (acrylic)
quotes.label: BASS-II report, abbreviations

quotes.quote: cast polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) samples were shaped as rods
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.5

terms.plain: cotton-fiberglass cloth
terms.def: SIBAL is a fabric of cotton on a fiberglass backing (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass by weight), named after an earlier NASA project, Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low Speeds.

quotes.quote: Sibal consisting of cotton on a fiberglass substrate (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass by weight)
quotes.label: PSI-98 Comment[Approach]

quotes.quote: The fabric is custom made for a previous project Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low Speeds (SIBAL)
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.94

terms.plain: near-weightless, like on the space station
terms.def: Microgravity is the near-weightless free fall of an orbiting spacecraft such as the International Space Station. Without buoyancy, hot gas does not rise, so flames change shape.

quotes.quote: flames in free fall (i.e., in microgravity) are often dramatically different because of the absence of buoyancy and thus rising hot gases
quotes.label: challenge page

quotes.quote: low-gravity combustion experiments, conducted for example on the International Space Station (ISS)
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: Moon or Mars gravity
terms.def: Partial gravity is gravity weaker than Earth's but far above zero, as on the Moon or Mars. PSI holds no fire data from it yet.

quotes.quote: there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: the airflow blew the flame out
terms.def: Blowoff: the flame goes out because the air flowing past it is too fast.

quotes.quote: blowoff extinctions
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.11

quotes.quote: consist of a blowoff and new quenching branch
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.66

terms.plain: the flame went out because the airflow was too weak
terms.def: Quenching: at very low airflow the flame becomes too weak to make up for the heat it loses, and goes out.

quotes.quote: quenching branch where the low power flame (due to the reduced temperature) is too weak to compensate for the surface radiative heat loss
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.66

terms.plain: the flame went out
terms.def: Extinction: the flame goes out. Blowoff (too much airflow) and quenching (too little) are two ways it happens.

quotes.quote: the flow speed at which the flames extinguished
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.74

terms.plain: the line between burns and doesn't burn
terms.def: A flammability boundary is the line, in oxygen and airflow, between conditions where a material keeps burning and where its flame goes out.

quotes.quote: O2-flow-velocity flammability boundary
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.94

quotes.quote: the flow speed at which the flames extinguished and the last flow speed at which a stable flame was obse
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.74

terms.plain: how hard the oncoming air strains the flame
terms.def: Stretch rate a (unit 1/s) measures how strongly the oncoming air strains the flame at the sample's tip. It rises with air speed and is larger for thinner rods: a = (3/2)(U/r)(r/r0)^0.5 (BASS-II eq. 6.1).

quotes.quote: The flammability map in terms of O2 and stretch rate a
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.66

terms.plain: oxygen per breath
terms.def: Oxygen partial pressure (pO2) is the part of the total pressure that comes from oxygen: O2 fraction x total pressure. Equal pO2 means each breath holds about the same amount of oxygen.

quotes.quote: Oxygen Partial Pressure and Oxygen Concentration Flammability
quotes.label: NTRS 20160001047

terms.plain: share of the air that is oxygen
terms.def: O2 % is the share of the gas that is oxygen, by volume (the same as mole %). Earth's normal air is 21% oxygen.

quotes.quote: a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen
quotes.label: PSI-20 Comment[Research Impacts]

quotes.quote: is the same as referring to it by its mole percent (21 mole % O2)
quotes.label: NTRS 20160001047 p.3

terms.plain: kilopascals, a unit of air pressure
terms.def: kPa (kilopascal) is a unit of pressure. Earth's air at sea level is 14.7 psi = 101.3 kPa (1 psi = 6.894757 kPa).

quotes.quote: the Earth’s pressure at sea level is 14.7 psi
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: Earth's sea-level air pressure
terms.def: 1 atm (one standard atmosphere) is defined as 101.325 kPa, Earth's average air pressure at sea level.

terms.plain: solid materials such as fabrics and plastics
terms.def: Solid materials: things like fabric and plastic, as opposed to gas or liquid fuels. NASA's flammability studies for crew cabins focus on them.

quotes.quote: Flammability studies focus on solid materials such as fabrics and plastics
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: the air planned for Moon bases
terms.def: Moon-base air: the atmosphere planned for Moon bases and pressurized rovers, 30% or more oxygen at 10.2 psi (70.3 kPa) or less, so astronauts can use spacesuits more easily.

quotes.quote: The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less
quotes.label: challenge page

quotes.quote: To facilitate spacesuit use, an atmosphere with increased oxygen and reduced pressure compared to Earth’s is expected within the planned Moon Base and pressurized rovers
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: NASA's public space-science data archive
terms.def: PSI (Physical Sciences Informatics, psi.nasa.gov) is NASA's public archive of physical-science experiments, including fire tests on the space station.

quotes.quote: are being made publicly available through NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database
quotes.label: challenge page

terms.plain: BASS-II, a fire experiment on the space station
terms.def: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II) burned small acrylic-plastic and fabric samples inside the space station's Microgravity Science Glovebox, varying the airflow and the oxygen.

quotes.quote: Main variables are airflow speed and oxygen concentration
quotes.label: PSI-25 Comment[Approach]

quotes.quote: the atmosphere in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)
quotes.label: BASS-II report p.3

terms.plain: Saffire, large fire tests in an uncrewed cargo spacecraft
terms.def: Saffire (Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration) burned large material samples inside Cygnus cargo spacecraft in orbit, to see how a large fire grows in low gravity.

quotes.quote: determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity
quotes.label: PSI-98 Comment[Objective]

quotes.quote: Microgravity (orbiting Cygnus) only
quotes.label: Saffire ICES-2024-365 (our summary)

terms.plain: SSCE, early fire tests on the Space Shuttle
terms.def: SSCE (Solid Surface Combustion Experiment) was the first combustion experiment flown on the Space Shuttle: flame spread over filter paper and acrylic plastic, over 8 flights.

quotes.quote: was the first combustion experiment to fly in the space shuttle
quotes.label: NTRS 20050177200

quotes.quote: the fuel sample--ashless filter paper
quotes.label: NTRS 20050177200

quotes.quote: a polymethyl methacrylate (plexiglass) fuel
quotes.label: NTRS 20050177200

quotes.quote: the final two of eight flights
quotes.label: NTRS 20050177200

terms.plain: air speed
terms.def: cm/s: centimetres per second, the speed of the air flowing past the sample (100 cm/s = 1 m/s).

terms.plain: keyword search
terms.def: BM25 is a standard keyword-ranking formula: passages that share more (and rarer) words with the question rank higher. No AI is involved in this step.
